coaching.headline: Six Fangtooth spawns, six takes, and they bought a comeback out of four losing lanes. The leak: a won map still took 45 minutes to close.
coaching.team: On paper only Steel's support matchup was ours, and the first twenty minutes read that way. The fights at their outer tower at 12 and 15.4 were lost 0-2 and 0-3. The defense of our own outer tower at 19.6 went 1-5, and deaths kept landing just before towers fell. What kept us alive was the trading. The losses at 12 and 19.6 each came with a Fangtooth taken in the same window. The loss at 25.5 came with Primal Fangtooth. We gave up bodies and took permanent stacks in return. The turn was three straight wins at our own objectives. The fight at our Primal Fangtooth at 27.2 was won 3-0. The fight at our inner tower at 29.2 was won 4-1 and cashed into Orb Prime at 30. Primal Fangtooth was defended again at 32.7, won 3-1. After that, the only concession of the entire game was the 36-minute Genesis Core, taken while Steel was dead. Two leaks survived the win. Five solo deaths came from players caught out alone, spread from 11.3 to 35.2 across Adele, Serath, The Fey and Steel twice. And the clock: we led objectives all game and let it run 45 minutes instead of converting the lead into an ending. Next game: when Orb Prime is taken, as it was at 30 and 41, the walk is straight at an inhibitor, all five together.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The stretch from 27.2 to 32.7 at our own Primal Fangtooth and inner tower turned it: three straight wins, 3-0 then 4-1 then 3-1, with Orb Prime cashed in the middle of it. The tower fights before that stretch had gone 0-2, 0-3 and 1-5. Same ten players, one change: we stopped fighting at their towers with lanes pinned and started fighting at our own objectives with all five alive.

perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Mr_Meat31 dealt 99,086 damage to heroes on a 9/4/15 line, and nobody else in the lobby broke 64,000. Mid was pinned early while the fights at 12 and 15.4 were lost. But the wins at our Primal Fangtooth at 27.2 and 32.7 were The Fey's fights. The catch by Rampage at 27.8, one minute after that first win, is the note: won fights are for cashing, not for walking off alone.
perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 took an offlane that read theirs all game and turned in 5/3/15 while soaking 65,837 damage. The early deaths were the expensive kind: the catch by Greystone at 11.3 came just before the outer tower fell at 11.7. The death at 15.4 came just before another tower at 16.6. From 27.2 on, Adele fought in all three of the straight wins that turned it: at our Primal Fangtooth, at our inner tower, and at Primal Fangtooth again.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's 57,308 objective damage carried the 12-tower count, on top of 9/6/10 in the fights and six-for-six on Fangtooth spawns — jungle tempo done right. The catch by Gideon at 24.9 is what made the defense at 25.5 a 4v5, and that is the one decision to take back.

The pattern to kill: two late solo catches, by Gideon at 30.7 and by Greystone at 35.2. The second came directly before the only major we conceded, the Genesis Core at 36, taken while Steel was dead. Steel also stayed in a winning lane while the push at their inhibitor at 34 was lost 2-3.

coaching.whatWorked: The Fangtooth record never slipped: every spawn of the game was taken. The Fangtooths fell at 8 and 14. The third came at 20. The Primals followed at 27 and 32. The last was at 41. Some were bought with lost fights — the tower losses at 12 and 19.6 each came with a Fangtooth taken in the same window. Trading bodies for permanent stacks is what kept four lanes we were losing on paper in the game.

19.6.call: Was the inner-tower defense at 25.5 worth a full engage with only four able to show? Primal Fangtooth fell to us in the same window, so the trade was already made. The better call was to concede the ground and reset with it rather than stand a 4v5 with the jungle down 36 seconds.

29.2.call: The right fight and the right follow-through: accept the engage at our own inner tower, win it, and walk straight onto Orb Prime while their timers ran. Cashing the win immediately instead of celebrating it is exactly the habit to keep.

45.1.call: The close finally came from committing to a structure instead of another fight — the right idea, executed two-strong into four defenders. Ending a game takes all five. With everyone walking in together, this push comes minutes earlier and never risks a flip.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Mr_Meat31's Fey build was the blueprint: Combustion for area burst, Wraith Leggings for penetration, Megacosm burning a slice of the target's maximum health, then Oblivion Crown multiplying the whole stack. The Tainted Scepter insert was the game-reading buy: its healing cut had two enormous targets, Rampage's 36,638 health healed and Maco's 28,847. The result, 99,086 hero damage, was the biggest total on either side of a 45-minute war, and a big part of why the late fights kept breaking our way.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Vesh multiplies a Fey who already tags whole teams: every area cast leaves a burn on everyone it touched, and the burn grows as games run long, exactly this 45-minute kind. Mind Rot keeps Greystone and Rampage from shrugging it off, and The Tenth Seal sharpens the ultimate. The trade stays what it always is for her, zero personal safety; four deaths says the team paid that bill so she could keep casting.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: Goldilocks324 built Adele like a heavyweight: Overlord's permanent health stacking, Rapture's on-hit damage with lifesteal, and Aegis Of Agawar's armor swell, then more armor and regeneration on top. Adele's listed core runs through Elafrost and Earthshaker instead, trading some of that bulk for a slowing empowered strike and ramping ability damage. Hard to argue with the outcome, 56,351 hero damage dealt while soaking 65,837 in the Greystone lane; the cost of the tank frame was pace, with Fist Of Razuul's healing empowered smash modeled online only around minute 41 of the 45.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Thraex is the dueling engine under that bruiser frame: Adele marks whoever she last hit, dealing more to them and taking less back, which is precisely the Greystone lane, two heavyweights refusing to leave. Ferocity stacks attack speed for as long as the brawl runs and Savage Strikes makes each swing carry extra sting. It gives up burst and any ranged answer; when the enemy kites instead of committing, the mark and the ramp both sit unused.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: Cuban Noobster nailed Serath's core and then read the game: Sky Splitter's current-health shred, Storm Breaker's chaining bolt, and Spectra's on-hit ramp for the attack-speed engine, then Tainted Rounds as the fourth buy. That healing cut was the most important purchase against this lineup: Rampage healed 36,638 health and Maco 28,847, and Serath is the one chasing them down. Draconum and Salvation closed with sustain and a shield for a jungler who absorbed 70,205 damage; a full-core build with the right situational spine.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Thraex feeds Serath's dive-and-stick pattern: mark the target she drops on, hit them harder, take less back, and let Ferocity's stacking attack speed carry the extended fight her lifesteal wants. Savage Strikes rounds out every swing. The trade-off is single-mindedness; it rewards committing to one target and gives nothing back when she has to swap off to peel for someone.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Willy Guggenheim ran Steel as a self-sufficient frame, armor, regeneration, and mitigation, and the reads inside it earned their keep: Tainted Guard cut the healing of whoever hit him, valuable against a Rampage who healed 36,638 health by brawling, and 76,725 damage taken bought the backline room all game. The standing critique still applies: Xenia's ally shield and Dynamo's take-more-damage debuff on stunned targets are how a Steel converts his crowd control into team kills rather than personal survival. In a won game that is a note about margin, not a verdict.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Vesh gives a frontline Steel a damage floor: every ability he lands, and his kit lands many, leaves a burn behind, with Mind Rot scaling it against the enemy's own tanks. The Tenth Seal adds punch to the level-10 ultimate. What it withholds is any help with the seven deaths, since the blessing neither shields nor heals him; it treats Steel's items as the armor and itself as the payback.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xeebs's Eden stacked the crit line: Vanquisher's execute, Imperator's bigger critical strikes, Dust Devil's attack-speed ramp, with Ashbringer refunding cooldowns on-hit and Viper shredding armor late. The listed core prefers Solaris and Nuclear Rounds, which push her ability damage and add an empowered healing strike, a steadier mix for a melee carry who dives. Ten kills and 49,014 hero damage say the crit route delivered; its cost is visible in the six deaths, an all-damage loadout with Terminus's overheal shield as the only cushion against a lineup led by Sparrow's 64k physical.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Vermis turns Eden's attack strings into tank-busting: every third hit on the same target takes a bite of their maximum health, Melting Point adds more against heavy armor like the enemy Greystone's, and Serration helps finish what her dashes start. It compounds a crit build neatly. The trade is the melee carry's usual one, nothing for the way in or the way out; the blessing assumes the frontline she jumps past stays busy elsewhere.

threats: Heal-stacking: Maco. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
synergy: Little hard CC on our side — we can't force a pick. Play for poke/objectives and punish their cooldowns, don't flip coin-toss 5v5s.
We have sustain (Adele, Steel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Bramble Patch slow → Harvest Nettles stacks → Untamed Growth DoT → Fly Trap pull ult
ourKits.winCondition: Fly Trap a clumped team and detonate AoE on the pull
ourKits.passive: takedowns spawn growths + grant move speed
ourKits.playWith: engage that clumps for her Fly Trap
ourKits.playAgainst: spread out vs the pull; she's squishy — dive her

ourKits.combo: Ascend dive → Heaven's Fury multi-strike → Chastise slow → Heresy form ult, resets on takedowns
ourKits.winCondition: dive the backline and snowball Heresy resets
ourKits.playWith: a frontline that creates her dive angle
ourKits.playAgainst: peel the backline — deny the first kill and her resets dry up

ourKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
ourKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
ourKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
ourKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

ourKits.combo: stance-swap with Zero Shift → Tachyon Lance (ranged) or melee chain → Limit Break on Overheat
ourKits.winCondition: build Heat and burst with Limit Break, flexing range and melee
ourKits.passive: damage builds Heat → Overheat unlocks Limit Break
ourKits.playWith: peel that lets her ramp Heat safely
ourKits.playAgainst: pressure her before Overheat; CC during the melee stance

enemyKits.combo: Pounce → Rumble slow → Boulder Throw → Behemoth ult to brawl
enemyKits.winCondition: engage with Pounce, grow with Behemoth and out-sustain the fight
enemyKits.passive: ramping health regen for jungle sustain
enemyKits.playWith: follow-up damage while he front-lines and CCs
enemyKits.playAgainst: anti-heal and kiting beat his sustain brawl; burst him before Behemoth

enemyKits.combo: Assault The Gates leap → Make Way armor shred → Sacred Oath empowered basic → Stone Forged Soul stasis ult
enemyKits.winCondition: front-line aggressively and reset the fight with the stasis heal
enemyKits.playWith: a team that fights while he soaks and stasis-resets
enemyKits.playAgainst: don't waste burst into his stasis — wait it out; anti-heal cuts the ult heal

enemyKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
enemyKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
enemyKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
enemyKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
enemyKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

enemyKits.combo: Piercing Shot poke → Heightened Senses AS → Hail of Arrows zone → Inner Fire ult
enemyKits.winCondition: ramp Relentless + AS and sustained-DPS the front down
enemyKits.playWith: heavy peel — she's immobile and pure DPS
enemyKits.playAgainst: she has zero escape — hard-engage her and she dies first

enemyKits.combo: Maco Gift! (heal ally / hurt enemy) → Maco Fly! slam → Maco Strike! charged line ult
enemyKits.winCondition: poke and heal-flex while landing the charged ult
enemyKits.playAgainst: dodge the charged Strike; pressure his low survivability
